subject: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniHealth pilot \u2014 next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@omnihealth.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@omnihealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniHealth pilot — next steps

Hi Taylor / Sam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you finish the vendor evaluation: 

Key pain points you reiterated:
- High 99th-percentile latency on existing inference endpoints causing poor clinician UX (esp. during peak hours).
- Rising per-token cost as call volume scales across multiple models and long-context document processing.
- Strict security requirements (audit logs + customer-managed keys) for PHI workloads.

Goals for the pilot:
1) Demonstrate consistent sub-200ms p95 latency for the summary use case at expected concurrency.
2) Show a 20-30% reduction in per-token cost using batching + prefix caching on your typical request mix.
3) Evidence of auditability: request/response logging and KMS integration in our private deployment.

Competitive landscape / decision criteria you mentioned:
- Latency & stability during peak hours (most important)
- Cost per normalized request at scale
- Security controls (KMS, audit logs)
- Ease of integration with your data plane and SSO for clinicians

Open questions we agreed to validate in the pilot:
- Can we run a 2-hour load test during your 10–12pm ET peak window?
- Confirmation of the anonymized prompt set and expected concurrency distribution (you to share)
- Procurement requirements and timeline for a POC contract (Sam to loop in procurement)

Proposed next steps:
- Onboarding runbook + scope doc (I attached our proposed bake-off scorecard and a short pricing comparison).
- Schedule load test for week of Mar 9 — I can coordinate with Marcus and Rishi for tuning during the window.
- Sam/Taylor to share sample prompt set + any non-PII pointer to clinical notes by EOD Mon, Mar 2.

Attachments: OMNI_Bakeoff_Scorecard.xlsx (scorecard), redwood-pricing-vs-competitors.pdf (high level comps)

If that aligns, I’ll put the load test on the calendar and send the onboarding packet.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@omnihealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@omnihealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@omnihealth.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniHealth pilot — next steps

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and the materials. This matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side before the load test: 

- We can share an anonymized sample prompt set by Mon EOD (we’ll strip PHI).
- Peak window for clinicians is usually 11:30–12:30 ET, but 10–12 is fine if that’s less disruptive.
- Procurement: we need a simple POC statement of work and a one-month trial price; I’ve CC’d procurement to start the paperwork.

Open items for Redwood to confirm:
1) Will you be able to provide KMS integration documentation and a sample audit log schema?
2) Can the test include one of your quantized model variants to show cost tradeoffs?

We’re happy to proceed — please send the onboarding packet and proposed SOW.

Cheers,
Taylor
Taylor Nguyen
Head of Product
OmniHealth
+taylor.nguyen@omnihealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniHealth pilot — next steps

Team — forwarding Omni’s reply and a quick internal plan. TL;DR: schedule load test week of Mar 9, need KMS/audit docs + ensure quantized variant is available for the run. 

Action items:
- Marcus: coordinate with infra on the 11:30–12:30 ET test window and set up the 2-hour load harness. Confirm whether we can include the int8 quantized variant without changing their integration surface.
- Rishi: prepare KMS integration guide + sample audit log schema. Also include brief notes on how prefix caching will be configured for their summary prompts.
- Lauren: I’ll need procurement language for a 1-month POC SOW and a recommended trial price (we discussed being aggressive to win the pilot).

I’ll draft the onboarding packet and send to Taylor once I have Marcus/Rishi inputs.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Competitive bake-off recap: OmniHealth pilot — next steps

Marissa / Rishi —

Quick update from infra: we can run the 2-hour load test on Thu, Mar 12 at 11:30–13:30 ET. We’ll provision a dedicated pool and instrument p95/p99 latency dashboards. Int8 quantized variant is available for the models they want to test; we’ll surface both quantized and float baselines in the scorecard. 

I’ll also include a short runbook for toggling batching/cache settings during the run so we can show the cost/latency tradeoffs live.

Marcus
